# Way Properties

<!-- GENERATED by tools/way_property_index.py --write. DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. -->
<!-- Source of truth: tools/way_properties.py. Run --check to verify the engine -->
<!-- has not drifted from it. -->

Every property a `way` node can carry, what it decides, and which code reads it.
A way has no single *kind*: its meaning is a point on four independent traversal
axes, plus metadata that has none. Most surprising doors are an unusual
combination of ordinary values, not a new value anywhere.

## The four traversal axes

These are independent of each other. Any combination is valid, which is why
`see_through` is not a kind of door — it is one axis among four.

- **passage** — Whether you can get through, and what stops you
- **transparency** — Whether you can see or hear through
- **verb** — Which movement verb the passage demands
- **size** — Who physically fits

Everything else in this page is either naming and layout (`identity`) or editor
metadata (`authoring`), neither of which changes what a character can do.

## Reading a way

```
current_state   does NOT let you through unless it is open
see_through    does NOT let you through, and does NOT stop light or sight
requires       which verb the passage demands (crawl / climb / jump)
max_size       who fits, relative to the character's size
```

Note that `movement.py` gates passage on `current_state` alone and never reads
`see_through`, while `barriers.py` resolves light and sound from `see_through`
*ahead of* `current_state`. That asymmetry is deliberate and is why a shut window
still lets light and sight through.

The combinations that come up most:

| what you want | how to say it |
|---|---|
| an open door | `current_state: open` |
| a door you can shut | `current_state: closed` |
| a window | `current_state: closed` + `see_through: true` |
| a glass door | `current_state: open` + `see_through: true` |
| an archway or trail you cannot shut | `open` + `prevent_close: true` |
| a glazed wall you must break | `closed` + `see_through: true` + `needs_open` |
| a crawlspace | `requires: crawl`, or `max_size` one tier under the character |

## Passage

_Whether you can get through, and what stops you._

| property | values | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `refusal_message` | — | Holds until the way is actually `open`. |
| `blocked_description` | — | Falls back to `refusal_message`. |
| `current_state` | `open`, `see_through`, `closed`, `locked`, `blocked`, `broken` | The passage ladder. Movement gates on THIS, never on see_through. |
| `one_way` | — | Incorporeal characters phase through it (task-309). |
| `auto_close` | — | Closes behind a character who has gone through. |
| `prevent_close` | — | Author's call, not the compiler's default. The state can then only be changed by triggers. An outdoor way carries it because you cannot close a road into a forest by hand. `requires: crawl/climb/jump` is always uncloseable independently of this. |
| `needs_open` | — | {enabled, skill, dc}. On a successful roll the way auto-sets current_state to 'open' and fires on_open triggers (engine/movement.py:582-600). This is how a closed, see-through wall becomes walkable — the 'break the glass' case. |
| `cost` | — | {time, energy}. 'time' is a DURATION HINT for a future stateful-action system, not per-action clock advancement — crawl/climb/jump do NOT scale costs today (task-187). |

### Read by

- `refusal_message` — `movement.py:572` — what a closed way says instead of letting you through
- `blocked_description` — `movement.py:1015` — why a blocked way is blocked
- `current_state` — `engine/barriers.py:135` — declared_state, normalised
- `current_state` — `engine/movement.py:564` — whether a traverse is refused
- `current_state` — `engine/barriers.py:148` — outranked by see_through for light and sound
- `one_way` — `engine/movement.py:558` — refuses the reverse traverse
- `prevent_close` — `engine/movement.py:1026` — character close is refused
- `prevent_close` — `engine/world_compile.py:411` — set on compiled outdoor ways

## Transparency

_Whether you can see or hear through._

| property | values | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `see_through` | — | The single transparency axis. Independent of current_state, which is why all four combinations of walkable/see-through are expressible: `closed` + see_through is a window, `open` + see_through is a glass door, `open` + prevent_close + see_through is an archway or trail. |
| `visible_in_direction` | — | Per-side, on the connection edge. Requires see_through to be seen. The auto-generated peek-through is NOT shown for see_through ways. |
| `sound_barrier` | — | Per-door override, applied while the way is solid (closed/locked/blocked only). Blank = the engine-config default. |
| `insulation` | — | A float multiplier on heat transfer across the way, default 1.0. A thick curtain or a shut door is how a cold room stays cold. |

### Read by

- `see_through` — `engine/barriers.py:148` — way_state returns see_through, outranking state
- `see_through` — `engine/barriers.py:44` — sound barrier 0.75 vs open 0.5
- `see_through` — `engine/barriers.py:62` — light transmission 0.75 vs open 1.0
- `see_through` — `engine/beyond_visibility.py:54` — line of sight continues through
- `see_through` — `engine/area_description.py:647` — peek-through text on examine
- `see_through` — `engine/awareness.py:159` — a quieter channel than open, louder than solid
- `see_through` — `static/js/agent/turn-feed.js:88` — a distinct sound cue
- `visible_in_direction` — `engine/area_description.py:723` — the 'what you see beyond' text
- `insulation` — `engine/environment_propagation.py:78` — multiplies the heat rate through this way

## Verb

_Which movement verb the passage demands._

| property | values | notes |

| `requires` | ``, `crawl`, `climb`, `jump` | crawl/climb/jump ways are always uncloseable. Failed climb and jump rolls fire on_fail_climb / on_fail_jump triggers. |
| `climb_dc` | — | Athletics DC when requires='climb'. Read as f'{requires}_dc', default 12. |
| `jump_dc` | — | Athletics DC when requires='jump'. Read as f'{requires}_dc', default 12. |

## Size

_Who physically fits._

| property | values | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `max_size` | `tiny`, `small`, `normal`, `huge`, `giant`, `titanic` | SIZE_TIERS is the whole model — engine/size.py:10 states there is no height or girth property. Carrying at >= 50% capacity adds one tier before the comparison (task-202), so a loaded character can be locked out of a gap they walked through unloaded. |
| `size` | — | On the CHARACTER, not the way (task-605). Read by way max_size gating and by per-area occupancy (task-653). Falls back to a `size_*` trait for hand-authored characters; the property must not default to 'normal' or it would silently outrank every trait and break the gate. |

### Read by

- `max_size` — `engine/movement.py:469` — two tiers over is blocked; one over crawls

## Identity

_Naming, layout and rendering — no traversal effect._

| property | values | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | — | Display only. Node identity is `id`, never the name. |
| `description` | — | Shown on examine and in look output while the way is solid. |
| `pass_message` | — | Overrides the generated KIND_MOVE_LINE when present. |
| `edge_length` | `20`, `500` | Graph spring length override. Not a traversal property. |
| `cardinal` | `north`, `northeast`, `east`, `southeast`, `south`, `southwest`, `west`, `northwest` | Per-side, on the connection edge. Decides map layout, not movement. |
| `physics_enabled` | — | Turn off to freeze the node while the rest of the graph settles. |
| `distance_from_parent` | — | Per-node graph physics distance. |
| `image` | — | Thumbnail on the graph when the Images toggle is on. |

### Read by

- `name` — `player.py:0` — what the player calls it
- `pass_message` — `movement.py:0` — narration line on a successful traverse

## Authoring

_Editor-facing metadata that changes how something is authored._

| property | values | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tags` | — | Identity matching; does not affect traversal. |
| `parameters` | — | {param:<key>} substitution in descriptions and trigger messages. |
| `aliases` | — | Other names that target this in commands. |
| `triggers` | — | on_open, on_fail_climb, on_fail_jump, requires_open, and the rest. |

## Known gaps

Declared or consumed somewhere, but not honored everywhere. Each needs a
decision, not just a note.

- **`current_state`** — `broken` is offered by the inspector's State dropdown but is NOT in engine/barriers.py WAY_STATES, and an unrecognised state resolves to UNKNOWN_STATE_FALLBACK = 'open'. If that holds, a broken door is more open than an open door. Verify, then either add it to both barrier tables in ladder order or remove it from the dropdown.
- **`see_through`** — engine/world_compile.py _mint_way hardcodes see_through=True on EVERY way it mints, so every painted door is currently glazed. Separate task.
- **`insulation`** — Was honored by engine/effect_handlers/ways.py alone; the library spawn, the refresh map and engine/sync.py omitted it, so a library-spawned way silently lost it. Fixed by task-659.

## The trigger spawn path is narrower

`engine/effect_handlers/ways.py` carries only 7 keys, because it assigns the rest
in its own props dict above the copy tuple. The checker does not hold it to the
same set, but these are read by the engine and are still unreachable there:

`blocked_description`, `climb_dc`, `jump_dc`, `refusal_message`, `sound_barrier`

Widening it is a feature decision rather than a drift fix.

## Where the compiler decides for you

A way the WorldPainter compiles is not authored by hand, so three behaviours come
from the grid rather than from a property.

- **Verticality is inferred, never declared.** `_climb_step`
  (`engine/world_compile.py`) turns a `floor` step over `DEFAULT_MAX_STOREY_STEP`
  (3, per-scope overridable) into a gated climb you cannot walk until a road is
  painted over it. A painted cell cannot declare "this is a climb". An interior
  opts out of the gate entirely by being an interior.
- **`CLIFF_FLOOR_DELTA` (2) is prose only** and `DEFAULT_MAX_STOREY_STEP` (3) is
  traversal. Adjacent constants, different jobs.
- **`_mint_way` hardcodes `see_through: True`**, so every painted door is glazed.
